findings.issue_text: [BUG] When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, minimumTokenResponseSchema strips the refresh_token and the fallback then writes the literal string "refresh_token" into the persisted credential key. For every service using parseRefreshTokenResponse (Google, Office365, Zoom) with credential sync enabled, the stored credential's refresh_token becomes the placeholder string "refresh_token" after one refresh, permanently breaking token refresh and forcing re-authorization for every affected user.

[BUG] The computed schema keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to the property name "[object Object]" (ZodString's default toString), so the schema validates nothing beyond access_token and the comment 'any property with a number is the expiry' is never realized. The 'minimum' schema silently drops every field except access_token, so consumers relying on expiry_date/instance_url/refresh_token in the parsed data (e.g. Salesforce instance_url, Google expiry_date) get undefined values written into prisma.credential records.

[BUG] googleCalendarService reads res?.data where res is the return of refreshOAuthTokens, but when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set that return is a fetch Response, which has no .data property. token becomes undefined and `googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` throws TypeError, so every Google Calendar operation fails with a 500 whenever credential sync is enabled — the documented happy path crashes.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response when the sync endpoint is used, but the caller treats it as an AxiosResponse (tokenInfo.data.error, tokenInfo.data.access_token). With credential sync enabled, tokenInfo.data is undefined and the subsequent property reads throw TypeError, breaking Zoho Bigin calendar operations entirely under the feature this PR introduces; same pattern in zohocrm CalendarService.ts.

[BUG] The sync-endpoint return (a fetch Response) is assigned to hubspotRefreshToken typed as HubspotToken, so .refreshToken/.expiresIn are undefined. With credential sync enabled, Hubspot persists undefined refresh_token and NaN expiry, silently corrupting the stored credential instead of the previous working OAuth refresh.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse with sharing enabled validates only against the minimum schema, so the persisted key keeps only access_token and loses instance_url, id, signature, and issued_at fields the jsforce Connection needs. Salesforce connections initialized after a sync-path refresh lose their instance_url/identity context stored in credential.key, producing broken API calls for Salesforce calendar users.

[ADVISORY] The Salesforce refresh now runs unconditionally in the service constructor path on every instantiation, with a remote POST to login.salesforce.com and a prisma.credential.update on each call. Every Salesforce calendar operation (including booking availability checks) now performs a network round-trip and DB write that previously only happened on token expiry via jsforce's built-in refresh, a hot-path latency and rate-limit regression.

[BUG] The error-handling branch is removed: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, but o365AuthCredentials was already spread with tokenResponse.data before any success check and the throw discards the previously logged MS response context. A Microsoft token error now surfaces as an opaque 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' 500 with the server response swallowed, degrading diagnosis of refresh failures that the old code logged.

[BUG] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws ZodError on invalid payloads, which is uncaught, producing a 500 instead of a 4xx. Any client posting a malformed body (e.g. userId as string) gets an unhandled server error; the JSON.parse of symmetricDecrypt output (line 59) similarly throws uncaught when the ciphertext is invalid or the key mismatch.

[ADVISORY] The handler performs no HTTP method check, so GET/DELETE requests with the secret in headers reach the body parse and Prisma paths. A GET /api/webhook/app-credential with valid headers returns a ZodError 500 rather than a 405; also the empty CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET default means if the env var is unset the check compares against undefined, and any request with a missing header matches (undefined === undefined) — though APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gating mitigates this.

[BUG] The parse target passed to parseRefreshTokenResponse is googleCredentials (the accumulated old credentials) rather than the freshly fetched token response, so when sharing is disabled the minimum-schema branch is skipped but in the enabled branch the stored key is validated against the wrong object. With sharing enabled, googleCredentialSchema (which would preserve the full credential shape) is never applied and only the fields present on the old googleCredentials plus a placeholder refresh_token are persisted, dropping any new fields from the provider.

[BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed keys, which evaluates to the literal property name "ZodString" (ZodString's toString), so the schema demands a numeric field literally named "ZodString" that no OAuth provider ever returns. Every credential-sync-mode refresh fails safeParse and throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', so the entire APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED feature never parses a single synced token response — the core new behavior is dead on arrival.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the ZodSafeParseResult wrapper object instead of the parsed data, and the sentinel `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` overwrites a real (or missing) refresh_token with the junk literal string 'refresh_token' for every caller in normal (non-sync) mode as well. Google CalendarService (CalendarService.ts:95) and Zoom (VideoApiAdapter.ts:104) store this wrapper / sentinel into prisma.credential.key; the next refresh uses refresh_token='refresh_token', which every provider rejects, permanently bricking the user's calendar integration after one token cycle.

[BUG] The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while every normal branch returns the provider SDK's parsed object (AxiosResponse for zoho-bigin/zohocrm, HubspotToken for hubspot, token object for google), so the function has incompatible return types and callers do `.data`/`.refresh_token` on the sync-path Response. In sync mode, zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts:92 `tokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError (Response has no .data); hubspot CalendarService.ts:181 reads `.refresh_token` off a Response getting undefined and stores NaN expiry; only webex/lark which pass the Response onward survive. Every sync-mode deployment crashes or corrupts credentials on first refresh.

[BUG] In sync mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse validates the accumulated googleCredentials object against the minimum schema (which, per the computed-key bug, always fails), and even on success the stored `key` is the safeParse wrapper — not googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) as before — so the persisted credential shape silently changes. Existing non-sync users' Google credentials get rewritten as a ZodSafeParseResult instead of the googleCredentialSchema shape; downstream code reading key.access_token finds undefined and calendar operations fail until the credential is reinstalled.

[BUG] The new code refreshes the Salesforce token on every SalesforceCalendarService construction using `response.statusText !== "OK"` as the error check, and the prisma.credential.update stores the parsed wrapper's `.data` with refresh_token — but the sync-mode path is never consulted (refreshOAuthTokens is not used here) and statusText is locale/HTTP-version dependent. Every calendar operation now performs an extra Salesforce token round-trip and a DB write (hot-path regression), and a 2xx response with a non-'OK' status phrase (e.g. HTTP/2 responses have empty statusText) throws HttpError 400, breaking all Salesforce integrations behind HTTP/2-capable fetch runtimes.

[BUG] symmetricDecrypt runs with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` and the result is fed to JSON.parse with no error handling, and the prisma.credential.update/create stores whatever JSON arrives without any schema validation. A payload encrypted with a wrong/stale key, or decrypting to non-JSON, throws an unhandled exception returning a 500, and a validly-encrypted but arbitrary JSON blob is written verbatim into credential.key, corrupting the user's integration with no schema check.

[ADVISORY] The new webhook endpoint, refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate have zero test coverage in this diff — no spec/test file touches any of the new files or the rewired CalendarService refresh paths. The computed-key zod bug and the safeParse-wrapper persistence bug (both guaranteed-failure modes of the new feature) would have been caught by a single unit test of parseRefreshTokenResponse; any regression in the 10 rewired refresh flows now ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The sync-mode fetch posts calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no timeout, no authentication header, and no response status check before returning the raw Response to callers expecting parsed tokens. A slow or failing self-hoster sync endpoint hangs every calendar/video operation (no AbortController timeout) and non-2xx responses flow into the type-mismatched callers, converting a third-party outage into booking failures for all users with synced apps.

[ADVISORY] The refactor removed the diagnostic branch that logged the zod error and MS response when parsing failed, replacing it with a throw inside parseRefreshTokenResponse that discards the underlying zod error and raw provider response. Operators debugging Office365 token refresh failures (a historically frequent MS API issue, per the deleted comment) now get only 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with no schema error or provider payload, making production triage materially harder.

[BUG] The Google refresh path now stores the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of the parsed credentials into prisma. `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns `{success, data, error}`, and `data: { key }` persists that wrapper object, so the stored credential key no longer matches googleCredentialSchema and every subsequent GoogleCalendarService instantiation fails schema validation, breaking Google Calendar for users whose token refreshes.

[BUG] When credential sync is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" on the parsed data. Callers (Google at CalendarService.ts:95 via `data: { key }`, Salesforce at CalendarService.ts:96) persist this literal into credential.key, so the next refresh sends "refresh_token" as the actual refresh token and OAuth refresh permanently fails with invalid_grant, losing the user's integration.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` collapse to a single literal key (zod objects stringify), so the schema does not "allow other properties" as commented and requires a property literally named after the stringified schema. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set, every token response whose keys don't include the accidental literal key fails safeParse and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', breaking all OAuth refresh under the feature this PR exists to implement.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when sync is enabled, but Hubspot treats the return value as a HubspotToken object. When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` / `.expires_in` are accessed on a Response object (undefined), so expiry math and subsequent API calls use NaN/undefined tokens and Hubspot integration calls fail.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response in sync mode but the caller reads `tokenInfo.data` (axios response shape). With sync enabled, `tokenInfo.data` is undefined, `!tokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError on reading `.error` of undefined, crashing the Zoho Bigin adapter.

[BUG] Same axios-vs-fetch Response type confusion: caller reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` on the Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens in sync mode. With sync enabled, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is undefined and reading `.error` throws TypeError, crashing Zoho CRM calendar operations.

[BUG] The Salesforce constructor now performs an unconditional token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com on every connection creation, replacing jsforce's on-demand refresh, and this change is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED or traceable to the sync requirement. Every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation (every booking/calendar operation touching Salesforce) performs a network round-trip and a credential DB write even when tokens are still valid, and unlike the other adapters it bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely, so the sync feature it was ostensibly added for doesn't even work for Salesforce; it also ignores HttpError import semantics by throwing on statusText !== 'OK' for non-200s.

[BUG] `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws an unhandled ZodError on invalid payloads, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on undecryptable input. Malformed or wrongly-encrypted webhook bodies produce an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx, and symmetricDecrypt with the empty-string fallback key when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset throws, crashing the handler despite the env var being nominally optional.

[ADVISORY] The call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication header, unlike the inbound webhook which requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Any party who can reach the self-hoster's sync endpoint can request token refreshes for arbitrary calcomUserId/appSlug pairs, and the endpoint (which holds app secrets per the .env.example description) is left unauthenticated; self-hosters deploying this get an unauthenticated credential-refresh oracle.

[ADVISORY] When sync is enabled the app-specific token schema is entirely discarded in favor of the 'minimum' schema, so app-specific fields (Google expiry_date, Salesforce instance_url/signature, Zoom token_type) are validated only by the broken minimum schema. Consumers of refreshed credentials (e.g. Salesforce jsforce Connection needing instance_url from the parsed data spread into the persisted key) receive unvalidated/missing fields in sync mode, producing downstream API failures that the pre-existing per-app schemas were there to catch.

[ADVISORY] This diff silently hardcodes the redirect URI slug `zoho-bigin` where `appConfig.slug` was used, an unrelated change to the config indirection. Anyone who changes zoho-bigin's slug in config.json (the pattern the config indirection exists for) now gets a redirect URI mismatch on OAuth start; also credentials-scope drift: the change is unrelated to credential sync and unexplained.

[ADVISORY] The comment instructs `openssl rand -base64 24` to generate a 32-byte key, but 24 base64-decoded bytes is 24 bytes, not the 32 required for AES256. Self-hosters who follow the comment generate a 24-byte key; symmetricDecrypt then fails (or silently mis-decrypts) on every inbound credential webhook, and the 403/500 that follows gives no pointer to the bad key length.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived solely from WEBHOOK_SECRET and ENCRYPTION_KEY being set, while CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (the third env var) is checked separately at every call site via `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` inline. The feature has two parallel enablement conditions scattered across files (constants flag + raw env read in refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse), so a future edit to one condition (e.g. also requiring the endpoint in the constant) silently desynchronizes which code paths take the sync branch — exactly the parallel-boolean drift that a single helper/config entry would prevent.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse sets a literal sentinel string "refresh_token" as the credential's refresh token whenever the parsed response lacks a refresh_token field. When credential sync is enabled the sync endpoint's response is validated against minimumTokenResponseSchema (which only requires access_token), so data.refresh_token is missing and gets overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token"; that value is then persisted to the credential row by every caller (Google, O365, Zoom, Salesforce) and used as the actual refresh token on the next refresh, permanently breaking token refresh for that credential with an unactionable provider error.

[BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema's two computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the same degenerate string key, so the 'any number property is the expiry' and 'allow other properties' fields the comments describe do not exist. The schema only ever enforces access_token and silently strips every other property (no expiry field is validated), so a malformed sync response missing expiry_date passes validation and downstream code writes undefined expiry, defeating the validation this helper was created to provide; the comments describe behavior the code does not implement.

[BUG] The zoho-bigin refreshOAuthTokens call passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but the parameter is `userId` and is sent as `calcomUserId` in the sync request body. When credential sync is enabled, the remote sync endpoint receives the credential's row id as calcomUserId, looks up the wrong (or no) user, and returns the wrong user's credentials or an error — token refresh silently operates on the wrong principal for every Zoho Bigin user.

[BUG] SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional network token refresh plus a credential DB write in the constructor path, and it does not route through refreshOAuthTokens, creating a parallel refresh path that ignores APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. Every Salesforce calendar operation now pays a synchronous round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a DB write even when the stored access token is still valid (previously jsforce refreshed lazily only on 401), a hot-path latency and rate-limit regression; and in the self-hosted-parent-app scenario this diff targets, the local Salesforce client_id/client_secret may not exist at all, so the constructor throws where the sync path was supposed to handle it.

[BUG] The sync-path fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication headers, no content-type, and no timeout, while the reverse-direction webhook (app-credential.ts) requires a CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header. A self-hoster who secures their sync endpoint with the documented webhook secret gets a 401/403 on every token refresh, and since refreshOAuthTokens propagates the raw error, every calendar/video operation for that app fails outright — the credential-sync architecture has no working auth contract in the outbound direction and no timeout bounds the cascading failure.

[ADVISORY] The credential write is a check-then-insert (findFirst then create) with no unique constraint on (userId, appId) backing it. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app race past the findFirst and both create a credential row, leaving duplicate credentials for the same app; later code that picks a credential by userId+appId gets nondeterministic behavior. A TOCTOU that only a DB unique index (or upsert on a composite key) closes.

[ADVISORY] The office365 path still checks `tokenResponse.success` and logs nothing, but parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on failure instead of returning an unsuccessful result, making the success check dead code and discarding the prior diagnostic logging. When the O365 token response is malformed, the operator now gets a bare 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with no MS response payload, and the `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` spread never runs its false branch — a debugging regression that bites whoever diagnoses the next Microsoft auth outage.

[ADVISORY] symmetricDecrypt is called with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""`, silently proceeding with an empty key when the env var is unset even though APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED can be true via CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET alone. A self-hoster who sets only the webhook secret gets credential-sync enabled but every webhook 500s (or decrypts garbage) on the empty key instead of a clear configuration error at startup or request validation — misconfiguration surfaces as per-request failures with encrypted-payload garbage.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result object, and GoogleCalendarService stores that entire object as the credential key. const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema) assigns a SafeParseReturnType (with .success/.data/.error fields) instead of the parsed credential, so prisma.credential.update writes a wrapper object to the key column — every subsequent Google credential read fails schema validation and Google Calendar booking breaks for all users, regardless of whether credential sharing is even enabled (the wrapper is returned on both code paths).

[BUG] When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, the function fabricates a literal refresh_token of "refresh_token" when the response omits one, and the Google call site then persists that fake value. The stored googleCredentials object gets refresh_token: "refresh_token" before being saved, so the next token refresh posts the literal string "refresh_token" to Google, permanently destroying the user's OAuth grant once credential sharing is enabled — silent, unrecoverable from Cal.com's side.

[BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys ([z.string().toString()]: z.number() and [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()), which zod evaluates to the string "[object Object]" / similar literal keys, so the schema only validates access_token and silently accepts nothing else. When credential sharing is enabled, a sync endpoint response missing expiry or containing garbage passes validation; Google then sets expiry_date from a nonexistent field (undefined), stores a credential that is both expired-per-logic and unexpired-per-data, and every calendar operation loops into re-refresh or fails.

[BUG] The synced branch returns a raw fetch Response while every call site other than lark expects the provider SDK's parsed shape (axios response or object), so the code immediately following dereferences fields that don't exist. HubspotCalendarService reads hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token on a Response (undefined→NaN expiry), Zoho Bigin/CRM read tokenInfo.data.error (TypeError crash), and Google reads res?.data (undefined→crash on token.access_token) — enabling CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT makes token refresh throw or corrupt stored credentials across five integrations.

[BUG] The refactor deleted the console.error logging of the zod failure and the MS response for invalid refreshed tokens, replacing it with parseRefreshTokenResponse which only throws when sharing is enabled. When credential sharing is disabled, a failed parse is now completely silent and the code still proceeds to prisma.credential.update with {...o365AuthCredentials, ...undefined-spread}, overwriting the stored O365 credential with whatever partially-validated data exists — a previously diagnosable failure mode becomes a silent credential corruption.

[BUG] The constructor now eagerly fetches a fresh Salesforce access token on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, whereas jsforce previously refreshed lazily on API use, and this path ignores refreshOAuthTokens/parseRefreshTokenResponse's shared sync branch. Every booking/query against Salesforce makes an extra unconditional network round-trip to login.salesforce.com (hot-path regression), a single failed refresh now fails the whole constructor before any operation, and Salesforce is inconsistent with every other integration: with sharing enabled it bypasses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT entirely, so synced instances never consult the parent app for Salesforce tokens.

[BUG] Success is checked via response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok or a parsed status code. fetch normalizes reason phrases; any HTTP/2 response (or a proxy) returns "" for statusText, so a successful 200 token refresh with empty statusText throws HttpError 400 and every Salesforce operation fails even though the token was valid.

[ADVISORY] The redirect URI was switched from the config-driven appConfig.slug to the hardcoded literal "zoho-bigin", breaking the single source of truth. If the app slug in config.json is ever changed or this block is copied for a new Zoho app (the established pattern), the OAuth redirect points at the wrong callback and the integration install flow 400s; the next change gets riskier because the constant now disagrees with the import two lines above it.

[ADVISORY] The handler runs zod .parse (not safeParse) on req.body with no method check and no try/catch, and reads the header name from an unvalidated env var. Any POST with a malformed body throws a ZodError outside the handler's control flow → unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx, and a GET request executes the full decrypt/DB-write path; a CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME containing underscores is silently dropped by Node's HTTP header normalization, making the endpoint reject all valid syncs with 403 while operators see no error.

[ADVISORY] The sync fetch sends no authentication (no webhook secret, no signature) to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, unlike the inbound webhook which requires a shared secret. Self-hosters who mirror the pattern get an unauthenticated outbound exchange of calcomUserId and appSlug (and implicitly the returned access tokens) — an attacker who learns the endpoint can request arbitrary users' tokens; this asymmetry between inbound and outbound trust will be copied as the documented integration contract.

[ADVISORY] The webhook shared secret is compared with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison. An attacker able to make repeated requests to /api/webhook/app-credential.ts can statistically recover the CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET byte-by-byte via response-time differences, then use it to overwrite any user's app credentials via the same endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted credential payload is JSON.parse'd and persisted verbatim as credential.key with no per-app schema validation, and the same static CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is shared by every request to this endpoint. Any party that obtains the single static secret (or a compromised parent application) can write an arbitrary JSON structure as any user's credential for any app (userId and appSlug are both caller-supplied with no per-user authorization), and downstream CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter code then consumes that attacker-shaped data as OAuth tokens.

[BUG] The outbound fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication (no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header, no TLS enforcement, no response verification), yet its response is returned as a token refresh result that gets parsed and persisted as the user's stored credential key. When credential sharing is enabled, every OAuth token refresh trusts an unauthenticated response from a config-controlled URL: anyone who can intercept or spoof that endpoint (plain HTTP, DNS hijack, on-path attacker) injects arbitrary token data that CalendarService writes to prisma.credential, hijacking the user's calendar/video account access.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to the literal property name "z.string()", so when credential sharing is enabled the schema validates nothing beyond access_token being a string. In sharing mode a token response missing expiry_date (or containing a non-numeric one, or any type for any field) passes validation and is persisted, and the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" is then written into the stored credential (e.g. zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts line ~104 stores parsedToken.data), so the user's real refresh token is destroyed and the next refresh sends the literal string to the provider, permanently breaking (and logging) that integration.

[BUG] The zod schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]:` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]:`, which collapse to a single literal property name (the string representation of the schema object), not a catch-all for 'any numeric property' or 'other properties' as the comments claim. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the minimum schema silently strips every field except access_token; callers that merge `tokenResponse.data` into credentials (office365, google) lose expiry_date, refresh_token, etc., corrupting stored credentials on every refresh. Additionally `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is never a declared field, so the `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token)` check at line 22 always fires and always overwrites with the sentinel string "refresh_token".

[BUG] When credential sync is enabled, the function returns the raw undici `fetch` Response object, but every call site was written against a parsed result type (google reads `res?.data`, hubspot expects `HubspotToken`, lark passes the value to `handleLarkError` expecting a fetch Response but with a Lark-shaped body, zoho expects an axios response with `.data`). In the Google CalendarService path, `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` followed by `res?.data` yields undefined, so `token.access_token` throws a TypeError on the very next line the first time a self-hoster enables sync — token refresh is broken in the synced configuration for every integration in this diff.

[BUG] The old code did `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (a plain credential object) and saved it; the new code assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` — a zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper `{success, data, ...}` — directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Every Google token refresh (even with sharing disabled) writes the zod result wrapper into the credential `key` column instead of the parsed credentials, so the next refresh reads `googleCredentials.refresh_token` from the corrupted shape and the integration breaks after a single refresh cycle.

[BUG] The function unconditionally defaults `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when absent, and its minimum schema never validates refresh_token's presence or shape. In the Google path the saved credential key gets `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`; the next refresh call passes that sentinel to `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...)`, producing a hard auth failure that a user cannot recover from without re-installing the app — a permanent credential poisoning triggered by one refresh under sync mode.

[ADVISORY] `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is unguarded, and `symmetricDecrypt` is called with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""`, so a wrong/missing key yields garbage or an empty-key decrypt that throws inside JSON.parse after the request was already authenticated. A self-hoster who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET but misconfigures or omits CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY gets an unhandled 500 (zod's `.parse` on line 21 likewise throws a raw 500 instead of a 4xx) instead of a diagnosable 4xx — the .env.example even documents generating a 24-byte base64 key whose decoded length may not be 32 bytes, making this misconfiguration easy to hit.

[BUG] When credential sharing is enabled the fallback `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` overwrites the real refresh token with the literal string "refresh_token", which is then persisted to `prisma.credential.update` by Google/Zoom/O365 callers. The provider's actual refresh_token is silently destroyed in the credential row; the next token refresh fails permanently and the user must re-authorize the integration — irreversible data loss with no rollback.

[BUG] `minimumTokenResponseSchema` builds its keys via `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluates to the literal string key "z.string()", so the schema requires a property literally named `z.string()` and z.object strips every real field (refresh_token, expiry, scope, instance_url) from the parsed data in sharing mode. In sharing mode every parsed token response loses all fields except access_token, and the stripped objects are written back to the credentials table (Google CalendarService writes `key` directly from this parse), silently dropping field-fidelity of stored credentials for all self-hosters with sync enabled.

[BUG] `refreshOAuthTokens` in sync mode returns a raw `fetch` Response, but the Google code reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, which is undefined on a Response object. `token.access_token` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` on every Google token refresh when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set; the sync feature can never work for Google Calendar and uncaught exceptions surface as 500s during booking flows.

[BUG] The result of `refreshOAuthTokens` is typed and used as `HubspotToken` but in sync mode it is a `fetch` Response, so `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, `.refreshToken`, and `.accessToken` are all undefined. HubSpot credential is persisted with `expiryDate = NaN` and garbage token fields, permanently corrupting the stored credential row (no rollback) for self-hosters with sync enabled; the previous valid tokens are overwritten.

[BUG] In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a `fetch` Response, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is undefined and the guard `!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` passes vacuously, then `data.access_token` etc. are undefined and get persisted to the credential. Zoho CRM credential rows are overwritten with undefined token fields, destroying the stored refresh-token payload and breaking the integration with no rollback path.

[BUG] `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `credentialId` as the third argument where every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the sync fetch (if it ever ran) would be sent the credential row id as calcomUserId, and the returned Response is consumed as an axios result (`tokenInfo.data.error`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse validates the accumulated googleCredentials object against the minimum schema (which, per the computed-key bug, always fails), and even on success the stored `key` is the safeParse wrapper — not googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) as before — so the persisted credential shape silently changes. Existing non-sync users' Google credentials get rewritten as a ZodSafeParseResult instead of the googleCredentialSchema shape; downstream code reading key.access_token finds undefined and calendar operations fail until the credential is reinstalled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes GoogleCalendarService to persist `key` as the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` instead of `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` (see `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); ... data: { key }`). But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the *Zod safeParse result object* (with `.success`/`.data`), not the parsed `.data`, so the persisted credential shape would become a `ZodSafeParseResult` wrapper, breaking downstream code expecting `credential.key.access_token`, etc. Additionally, in “sync mode” it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` which is incorrectly defined with computed keys (`[z.string().toString()]` etc.), making the schema effectively require a literal property name like "[object Object]" and thus likely fail validation and throw. Both issues are directly evidenced in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` and its new call sites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new code refreshes the Salesforce token on every SalesforceCalendarService construction using `response.statusText !== "OK"` as the error check, and the prisma.credential.update stores the parsed wrapper's `.data` with refresh_token — but the sync-mode path is never consulted (refreshOAuthTokens is not used here) and statusText is locale/HTTP-version dependent. Every calendar operation now performs an extra Salesforce token round-trip and a DB write (hot-path regression), and a 2xx response with a non-'OK' status phrase (e.g. HTTP/2 responses have empty statusText) throws HttpError 400, breaking all Salesforce integrations behind HTTP/2-capable fetch runtimes.

[BUG] symmetricDecrypt runs with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""` and the result is fed to JSON.parse with no error handling, and the prisma.credential.update/create stores whatever JSON arrives without any schema validation. A payload encrypted with a wrong/stale key, or decrypting to non-JSON, throws an unhandled exception returning a 500, and a validly-encrypted but arbitrary JSON blob is written verbatim into credential.key, corrupting the user's integration with no schema check.

[ADVISORY] The new webhook endpoint, refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and the APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate have zero test coverage in this diff — no spec/test file touches any of the new files or the rewired CalendarService refresh paths. The computed-key zod bug and the safeParse-wrapper persistence bug (both guaranteed-failure modes of the new feature) would have been caught by a single unit test of parseRefreshTokenResponse; any regression in the 10 rewired refresh flows now ships undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s “guaranteed-failure modes” are grounded in the diff: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` is defined with computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()`, which becomes a literal property name (e.g., "ZodString") rather than a dynamic key pattern, so the schema will not accept real token responses and will likely make `safeParse` fail when credential sharing is enabled. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the *safeParse result object*, but `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` assigns that directly to `key` and persists it (`data: { key }`), which would store `{success, data,...}` instead of the credential payload. While the comment about missing tests is plausible (no test/spec files appear in this diff), the diff also shows real functional defects, so this is a bug finding rather than purely “missing coverage”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-mode fetch posts calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no timeout, no authentication header, and no response status check before returning the raw Response to callers expecting parsed tokens. A slow or failing self-hoster sync endpoint hangs every calendar/video operation (no AbortController timeout) and non-2xx responses flow into the type-mismatched callers, converting a third-party outage into booking failures for all users with synced apps.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), does `fetch(...)` and **returns the raw `Response` object** without checking `response.ok` or parsing JSON (`apps-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Callers were updated to assume the returned value is already the provider token response shape (or at least has `.data`), e.g. Google Calendar: `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` (now `res` would be a Fetch `Response` with no `.data`), leading to `token` being `undefined` and subsequent `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date` access failing. Similar type/shape mismatches exist in other integrations that expect parsed objects/axios-like responses. The lack of timeout and status checking further exacerbates hanging/failing behavior as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refactor removed the diagnostic branch that logged the zod error and MS response when parsing failed, replacing it with a throw inside parseRefreshTokenResponse that discards the underlying zod error and raw provider response. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` branch that logged `tokenResponse.error` and the raw `responseJson` on failure was removed. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Google refresh path now stores the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of the parsed credentials into prisma. `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` returns `{success, data, error}`, and `data: { key }` persists that wrapper object, so the stored credential key no longer matches googleCredentialSchema and every subsequent GoogleCalendarService instantiation fails schema validation, breaking Google Calendar for users whose token refreshes.

[BUG] When credential sync is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" on the parsed data. Callers (Google at CalendarService.ts:95 via `data: { key }`, Salesforce at CalendarService.ts:96) persist this literal into credential.key, so the next refresh sends "refresh_token" as the actual refresh token and OAuth refresh permanently fails with invalid_grant, losing the user's integration.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed token data lacks `refresh_token`, the function unconditionally assigns the literal string `"refresh_token"` (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`). This can overwrite/introduce an invalid refresh token value that callers may persist back into `prisma.credential.key` (e.g., Office365 merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and updates the credential). However, the finding’s specific examples are partly incorrect: Salesforce explicitly persists the old refresh token (`refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token`), and Google’s code actually appears to persist the entire zod parse result object (`key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` then `data: { key }`), which is a separate (and likely worse) bug than the refresh_token literal overwrite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` collapse to a single literal key (zod objects stringify), so the schema does not "allow other properties" as commented and requires a property literally named after the stringified schema. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set, every token response whose keys don't include the accidental literal key fails safeParse and the function throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned', breaking all OAuth refresh under the feature this PR exists to implement.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed property names evaluate immediately to string literals (e.g., the `toString()` of a Zod schema), and both likely stringify to the same key, so one overwrites the other. This does not create an index signature / “allow other properties”; instead it creates (and requires) a single specific property name. Under `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, `safeParse(response)` will therefore fail for normal OAuth token responses that don’t include that accidental literal key, causing `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to throw and breaking refresh flows added in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when sync is enabled, but Hubspot treats the return value as a HubspotToken object. When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` / `.expires_in` are accessed on a Response object (undefined), so expiry math and subsequent API calls use NaN/undefined tokens and Hubspot integration calls fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, it calls `fetch(...)` and returns that raw `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result is typed/used as `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`) and the subsequent logic (shown starting with `// set expiry date as offset from current time.`) expects token fields like `expires_in` / `refresh_token` on that value. When sync is enabled, those properties will not exist on a `Response`, causing undefined/NaN expiry calculations and breaking the Hubspot integration refresh flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response in sync mode but the caller reads `tokenInfo.data` (axios response shape). With sync enabled, `tokenInfo.data` is undefined, `!tokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError on reading `.error` of undefined, crashing the Zoho Bigin adapter.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result is stored as `tokenInfo` and then accessed as `tokenInfo.data` (axios response shape): `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`. If sync mode is triggered, `tokenInfo` will be a `Response` (no `.data`), so `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `tokenInfo.data.error` will throw a TypeError, crashing the adapter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Same axios-vs-fetch Response type confusion: caller reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` on the Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens in sync mode. With sync enabled, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is undefined and reading `.error` throws TypeError, crashing Zoho CRM calendar operations.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is assigned from `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then used as an Axios response: `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a `fetch(...)` Response when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. A Fetch `Response` does not have a `.data` property, so in sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `.error` access will throw a `TypeError`, breaking Zoho CRM token refresh / calendar operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Salesforce constructor now performs an unconditional token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com on every connection creation, replacing jsforce's on-demand refresh, and this change is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED or traceable to the sync requirement. Every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation (every booking/calendar operation touching Salesforce) performs a network round-trip and a credential DB write even when tokens are still valid, and unlike the other adapters it bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely, so the sync feature it was ostensibly added for doesn't even work for Salesforce; it also ignores HttpError import semantics by throwing on statusText !== 'OK' for non-200s.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs a refresh-token `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` unconditionally before constructing the `jsforce.Connection`. This is not gated by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, unlike other adapters in the diff, so it will cause a network round-trip + DB write on every service instantiation even when not needed and does not integrate with the sync endpoint logic. Additionally, error handling checks `response.statusText !== "OK"` rather than `response.ok`/status code, which is brittle for non-200 responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws an unhandled ZodError on invalid payloads, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on undecryptable input. Malformed or wrongly-encrypted webhook bodies produce an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx, and symmetricDecrypt with the empty-string fallback key when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset throws, crashing the handler despite the env var being nominally optional.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is called without a try/catch (or `safeParse`), so an invalid body will throw a `ZodError` and bubble up as a 500. Likewise, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` is unguarded, so malformed ciphertext / wrong key / non-JSON plaintext will also throw and produce a 500 instead of a controlled 4xx. However, the finding’s claim about crashing when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset is not supported because the handler returns early when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is falsy, and that constant is only truthy when both `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are set (see `packages/lib/constants.ts`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication header, unlike the inbound webhook which requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Any party who can reach the self-hoster's sync endpoint can request token refreshes for arbitrary calcomUserId/appSlug pairs, and the endpoint (which holds app secrets per the .env.example description) is left unauthenticated; self-hosters deploying this get an unauthenticated credential-refresh oracle.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `refreshOAuthTokens` calling `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth header or shared-secret/signature (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). While the finding’s claim about the *self-hoster’s* endpoint being unauthenticated can’t be verified from this PR (that endpoint’s implementation is خارج the diff), it is a concrete, diff-grounded security/design gap that Cal.com provides no built-in way to authenticate its outbound refresh calls (unlike the new inbound webhook which checks `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When sync is enabled the app-specific token schema is entirely discarded in favor of the 'minimum' schema, so app-specific fields (Google expiry_date, Salesforce instance_url/signature, Zoom token_type) are validated only by the broken minimum schema. Consumers of refreshed credentials (e.g. Salesforce jsforce Connection needing instance_url from the parsed data spread into the persisted key) receive unvalidated/missing fields in sync mode, producing downstream API failures that the pre-existing per-app schemas were there to catch.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly bypasses the per-app token schema when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, using `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` instead of the provided `schema` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). That means app-specific required fields are no longer validated in sync mode. This is concretely problematic in the diff: Salesforce now persists refreshed credentials from `accessTokenParsed.data` (`...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ...`) and then uses them to construct a jsforce Connection, which depends on fields like `instance_url` (see `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`), but in sync mode those fields are not guaranteed/validated by the minimum schema and may be missing, causing downstream failures. The finding’s core claim (schema discarded → missing/unvalidated fields in sync mode) is directly supported by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This diff silently hardcodes the redirect URI slug `zoho-bigin` where `appConfig.slug` was used, an unrelated change to the config indirection. Anyone who changes zoho-bigin's slug in config.json (the pattern the config indirection exists for) now gets a redirect URI mismatch on OAuth start; also credentials-scope drift: the change is unrelated to credential sync and unexplained.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts`, the redirect URI was changed from `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to the hardcoded `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback``. This removes the existing config indirection (`appConfig.slug`) and creates a potential mismatch if `config.json`'s `slug` is ever changed. However, from the diff alone we can't verify that `appConfig.slug` is currently different from `"zoho-bigin"`, so it's not a demonstrable breakage today—it's a concrete maintainability/consistency regression and scope drift relative to the credential-sync changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The comment instructs `openssl rand -base64 24` to generate a 32-byte key, but 24 base64-decoded bytes is 24 bytes, not the 32 required for AES256. Self-hosters who follow the comment generate a 24-byte key; symmetricDecrypt then fails (or silently mis-decrypts) on every inbound credential webhook, and the 403/500 that follows gives no pointer to the bad key length.

adjudication.rationale: In `.env.example` the new comment says `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` “must be 32 bytes for AES256” but then recommends `openssl rand -base64 24`, which generates 24 random bytes (base64-encoded), not 32. The misleading guidance is directly verifiable in the diff. However, the claim that `symmetricDecrypt` will fail or silently mis-decrypt with a 24-byte key isn’t verifiable from this diff alone (the crypto implementation isn’t shown), so the concrete, diff-grounded issue is incorrect documentation/misconfiguration guidance rather than a proven code defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived solely from WEBHOOK_SECRET and ENCRYPTION_KEY being set, while CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (the third env var) is checked separately at every call site via `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` inline. The feature has two parallel enablement conditions scattered across files (constants flag + raw env read in refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse), so a future edit to one condition (e.g. also requiring the endpoint in the constant) silently desynchronizes which code paths take the sync branch — exactly the parallel-boolean drift that a single helper/config entry would prevent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` in `packages/lib/constants.ts` as truthy when `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are set, but the actual “sync branch” behavior in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` additionally requires `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (checked inline at each call). This creates two related but different enablement conditions (flag vs. flag+endpoint) spread across files, so changing one condition later could desynchronize behavior as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse sets a literal sentinel string "refresh_token" as the credential's refresh token whenever the parsed response lacks a refresh_token field. When credential sync is enabled the sync endpoint's response is validated against minimumTokenResponseSchema (which only requires access_token), so data.refresh_token is missing and gets overwritten with the literal string "refresh_token"; that value is then persisted to the credential row by every caller (Google, O365, Zoom, Salesforce) and used as the actual refresh token on the next refresh, permanently breaking token refresh for that credential with an unactionable provider error.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse assigns the literal string "refresh_token" when the response lacks a refresh_token field, causing an invalid refresh token to be stored and used on subsequent refresh attempts, leading to authentication/token refresh failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema's two computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the same degenerate string key, so the 'any number property is the expiry' and 'allow other properties' fields the comments describe do not exist. The schema only ever enforces access_token and silently strips every other property (no expiry field is validated), so a malformed sync response missing expiry_date passes validation and downstream code writes undefined expiry, defeating the validation this helper was created to provide; the comments describe behavior the code does not implement.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to strings (very likely the same string, e.g. a schema stringification), so they do not create “any number property” / “allow other properties” behavior. With `z.object(...)`’s default unknown-key stripping, fields like `expiry_date` are not validated (and may be stripped), meaning a malformed sync response missing expiry info can pass the “minimum” validation contrary to the comments/intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zoho-bigin refreshOAuthTokens call passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but the parameter is `userId` and is sent as `calcomUserId` in the sync request body. When credential sync is enabled, the remote sync endpoint receives the credential's row id as calcomUserId, looks up the wrong (or no) user, and returns the wrong user's credentials or an error — token refresh silently operates on the wrong principal for every Zoho Bigin user.
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same bug: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `credentialId` where `userId` is expected, causing incorrect user lookups during credential sync and leading to sync failures or wrong credentials being used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional network token refresh plus a credential DB write in the constructor path, and it does not route through refreshOAuthTokens, creating a parallel refresh path that ignores APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. Every Salesforce calendar operation now pays a synchronous round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a DB write even when the stored access token is still valid (previously jsforce refreshed lazily only on 401), a hot-path latency and rate-limit regression; and in the self-hosted-parent-app scenario this diff targets, the local Salesforce client_id/client_secret may not exist at all, so the constructor throws where the sync path was supposed to handle it.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now unconditionally calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then immediately performs `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (see the newly added block starting at `const response = await fetch(...)` through the `await prisma.credential.update(...)`). There is no guard on token validity/expiry, so constructing/initializing the service always forces a network round-trip and DB write. Also, unlike the other integrations changed in this PR, Salesforce does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so the credential-sync path (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) is bypassed entirely for Salesforce, which directly contradicts the new intended behavior in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync-path fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication headers, no content-type, and no timeout, while the reverse-direction webhook (app-credential.ts) requires a CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header. A self-hoster who secures their sync endpoint with the documented webhook secret gets a 401/403 on every token refresh, and since refreshOAuthTokens propagates the raw error, every calendar/video operation for that app fails outright — the credential-sync architecture has no working auth contract in the outbound direction and no timeout bounds the cascading failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync-path `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` does not include any authentication header or timeout/abort handling, so a self-hoster securing that endpoint would indeed get 401/403 and the caller code would then fail downstream. However, the diff does not establish that `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is supposed to accept the same `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` used by the *incoming* webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), and the comment explicitly says “Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires”, so the claimed “documented webhook secret” contract mismatch is not strictly verifiable from the diff. Also, the claim of “no content-type” is likely inaccurate because `fetch` with a `URLSearchParams` body typically sets `application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8` automatically. The lack of an outbound auth/timeout contract is still a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/architecture gap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The credential write is a check-then-insert (findFirst then create) with no unique constraint on (userId, appId) backing it. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app race past the findFirst and both create a credential row, leaving duplicate credentials for the same app; later code that picks a credential by userId+appId gets nondeterministic behavior. A TOCTOU that only a DB unique index (or upsert on a composite key) closes.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId }})` and then conditionally calls `prisma.credential.create(...)` if none is found. This is a classic check-then-insert pattern that can race under concurrent webhook deliveries; without a transactional upsert or a DB-enforced unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`, duplicates could be created. The diff does not show the Prisma schema/migrations, so the claim that there is definitively "no unique constraint" is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the TOCTOU risk in the handler code is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The office365 path still checks `tokenResponse.success` and logs nothing, but parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on failure instead of returning an unsuccessful result, making the success check dead code and discarding the prior diagnostic logging.
