adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The result of `refreshOAuthTokens` is typed and used as `HubspotToken` but in sync mode it is a `fetch` Response, so `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`, `.refreshToken`, and `.accessToken` are all undefined. HubSpot credential is persisted with `expiryDate = NaN` and garbage token fields, permanently corrupting the stored credential row (no rollback) for self-hosters with sync enabled; the previous valid tokens are overwritten.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a `Response` object, not the app-specific token shape. But in `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned value is typed/used as `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`). In sync mode this will be a `Response`, so downstream code that reads token fields (implied by the existing flow: “set expiry date as offset...”) will see `undefined` values and can compute invalid expiry/token fields and persist them. The diff does not add any parsing (like the new `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) for HubSpot to convert a `Response` into token data, so the mismatch is introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a `fetch` Response, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is undefined and the guard `!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` passes vacuously, then `data.access_token` etc. are undefined and get persisted to the credential. Zoho CRM credential rows are overwritten with undefined token fields, destroying the stored refresh-token payload and breaking the integration with no rollback path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zohocrm", credential.userId)` and then treats the result as an Axios response (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data...`). But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` object in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), which does not have a `.data` property. This will break at runtime (likely a `TypeError` when evaluating `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`). The finding’s specific claim that the guard “passes vacuously” and that undefined tokens get persisted isn’t directly shown in the diff, but the underlying type/behavior mismatch introduced by the diff is real and verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `credentialId` as the third argument where every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the sync fetch (if it ever ran) would be sent the credential row id as calcomUserId, and the returned Response is consumed as an axios result (`tokenInfo.data.error`). The sync endpoint receives a credential id instead of the user id, so any credential it creates/updates is keyed to the wrong user; combined with the Response/axios shape mismatch the stored Bigin credential is corrupted.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens` is invoked as `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. The helper’s third parameter is `userId: number | null` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) and all other updated call sites pass `credential.userId`. Passing `credentialId` (by name, strongly suggesting the credential row id, not the user id) would send the wrong `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. Additionally, when syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`, but the Bigin code treats the result as an axios response (`tokenInfo.data.error`), which would break/corrupt the refresh flow under the sync path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new unconditional Salesforce token refresh gate `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` relies on statusText, which is empty for HTTP/2 responses and non-"OK" for many 200s, and the credential overwrite runs in the service constructor on every instantiation. Every Salesforce calendar/video operation now performs an extra remote token refresh on the hot path and throws HttpError 400 on valid responses with empty statusText (HTTP/2), breaking all Salesforce integrations for those deployments; when it does succeed it overwrites the credential key on every construction.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now unconditionally performs a refresh-token HTTP request and credential DB update as part of creating the jsforce connection (code added immediately before `return new jsforce.Connection(...)`). This means every instantiation pays an extra remote call and overwrites the stored credential key. Additionally, the error gate `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` is based on `statusText` rather than `response.ok`/`response.status`, so it can throw even on successful 2xx responses where `statusText` is empty or not exactly "OK".

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` are unguarded, so any malformed body or unset encryption key throws. A malformed webhook payload or a deployment where CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset crashes with an unhandled 500 (symmetricDecrypt with empty key throws) instead of the 4xx the endpoint contract implies, and the failure occurs before the user/app existence guards.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is not wrapped in a try/catch (nor uses `safeParse`), so any malformed/invalid webhook body will throw and result in an unhandled 500 rather than a 4xx response. Similarly, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can throw (bad ciphertext / non-JSON plaintext), also yielding a 500. However, the finding’s claim that an *unset* `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` crashes is not supported by the diff because the handler returns 403 early when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is falsy, and that constant is derived from the presence of `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is derived solely from the presence of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY with no dedicated feature flag, and it silently reroutes all OAuth token refreshes through a third-party endpoint once both are set. Self-hosters who set the webhook secret for the credential-receive webhook alone accidentally redirect every app's token refresh away from the real provider, corrupting credentials per the parseRefreshTokenResponse defects; there is no way to disable the reroute without an env change and redeploy/restart.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OAuth refresh rerouting only happens when **all** of these are true: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (derived from `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` && `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in `packages/lib/constants.ts`), **and** `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, **and** `userId` is non-null (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). The finding claims setting the webhook secret alone would “silently reroute all OAuth token refreshes,” which is not supported by the code (it also requires the encryption key and the sync endpoint, and only applies when `userId` exists). Claims about “corrupting credentials per the parseRefreshTokenResponse defects” are also not directly verifiable from the diff as a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The value persisted to the credential is the entire Zod safeParse result wrapper, not the parsed data. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}); previously the code used googleCredentialSchema.parse() which returned the data object. prisma.credential.update now writes `{success: true, data: {…}}` as the credential key, so the very next calendar operation decodes a key with no access_token at the top level and Google Calendar integration breaks for every user on token refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error? }`), not the parsed `data` itself. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credential is now persisted via `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` followed by `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This writes the wrapper object into `credential.key` rather than the expected token payload (previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the payload). That would change the stored shape so later code reading `credential.key` as token fields (e.g., `access_token` at top level) would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response but the Google code reads `res?.data`. The non-sharing path returns the googleapis lib result (which has .data); the sharing path returns a WHATWG Response, so `token = res?.data` is always undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError inside refreshAccessToken, so every Google token refresh fails on any self-hosted deployment with CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it does `return response;` where `response` is a WHATWG `fetch` `Response`. But in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller assumes an axios/googleapis-style response and does `const token = res?.data;` followed by `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date`. A WHATWG `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime on the sharing-enabled path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so the schema validates only `access_token` and Zod's default strip mode drops every other field (expiry, instance_url, refresh_token) from the parsed data. Every caller using the sharing path (O365, Zoom, Salesforce, Google) receives data containing only access_token; e.g. Office365CalendarService spreads `tokenResponse.data` and silently loses expires_in, so expiry is never updated, the token is re-refreshed on every call, and Salesforce's stored key loses instance_url/signature making the persisted credential unusable for subsequent jsforce calls.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to the literal key string `"[object Object]"` (and the latter overwrites the former). As a result, when the “sharing path” is active (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), the schema effectively validates only `access_token` (plus an irrelevant optional `"[object Object]"` key) and Zod’s default object behavior strips all other fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, etc.) from `data`. The function then also forces `refresh_token` to a placeholder if missing. Call sites shown in the diff (e.g., Office365 spreading `tokenResponse.data`, Salesforce persisting `{...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ...}`, Zoom using the parsed result) would therefore lose required token metadata and can persist incomplete credentials or fail to update expiry, matching the finding’s described broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A missing refresh_token is backfilled with the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted to the credential. After the first sharing-path refresh (which strips fields per the schema bug, including refresh_token), the credential's refresh_token becomes the string "refresh_token"; the next refresh sends that garbage to the provider and the integration is permanently bricked with no error surfaced at write time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, parses the refresh response with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` that does not include `refresh_token`, and then forcibly backfills `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` if missing (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). At least one caller persists this into the stored credential: Office365 merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and then writes it via `prisma.credential.update`, so the real refresh token can be replaced by the literal string "refresh_token" under the sharing path (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). This can brick subsequent refreshes by sending an invalid refresh token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With credential sharing enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response but the code treats it as a HubspotToken object. `hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in` is undefined on a Response, so expiry_date is computed as `Date.now() + undefined*1000` = NaN and the NaN/undefined-bearing key is written to the credential via prisma update, corrupting the stored Hubspot credential silently while the operation reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(..., "hubspot", credential.userId)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a `fetch(...)` **Response** when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, not a parsed token object. The Hubspot code still expects a `HubspotToken` shape (e.g., `expires_in` etc., as indicated by the immediately following comment about computing expiry), so with credential sharing enabled it will read properties off a `Response`, producing `undefined`/invalid values and leading to incorrect expiry computation and subsequent credential persistence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With credential sharing enabled, tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so `tokenInfo.data.error` and `tokenInfo.data.expires_in` are undefined and the code treats the call as success. A failed sync-endpoint response (fetch never throws on HTTP errors, and refreshOAuthTokens never checks response.ok) is reported as a successful refresh; expiryDate is set to `Date.now() + undefined` = NaN and the corrupted key is persisted, bricking the Zoho Bigin credential.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it always does a `fetch(...)` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and returns the raw `Response` without checking `response.ok` or parsing JSON. In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code assigns `const tokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then treats it like an Axios response (`tokenInfo.data.error`, and later presumably uses `tokenInfo.data.expires_in`). If the sharing branch is taken, `tokenInfo` is a Fetch `Response` (no `.data`), so this will break at runtime (TypeError accessing `tokenInfo.data.error`) and/or lead to undefined fields. This mismatch is introduced by the diff and is a real correctness defect under the new credential-sharing path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` with no error wrapper, so any invalid payload throws an unhandled ZodError. A malformed webhook body (wrong types, missing userId) returns a raw 500 with a stack-bearing error instead of the 400 the webhook contract implies, and the caller cannot distinguish a validation problem from a server outage. The same applies to `symmetricDecrypt` at line 55 with an unset/short CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which throws and 500s.
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags that `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` can throw an unhandled ZodError on invalid payloads, causing 500 responses instead of an intended 400 for bad requests, which is the same core issue as the golden comment. It also adds an extra related throw case (`symmetricDecrypt`), but that doesn’t change the match on the primary issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout and its result is returned without checking response.ok. A hung or slow self-hoster sync endpoint stalls every calendar/video token refresh indefinitely (booking flows hang on the request path), and a 4xx/5xx response is passed through to callers that parse the body, producing cryptic JSON parse errors instead of a refresh-specific error message.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and directly `return response;` with no timeout/abort mechanism and no `response.ok` / status handling. This can hang token refresh indefinitely on slow endpoints and passes through non-2xx responses to callers that then try to parse/use the body (e.g., `handleErrorsJson(response)` or accessing `res.data` in Google), leading to opaque downstream errors rather than a clear refresh failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Success is checked via `response.statusText !== "OK"` and the subsequent `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is dead code. statusText is not a reliable success indicator (HTTP/2 fetches commonly return an empty statusText), so real failures can slip past as 400s with the wrong message or, when they don't, the parse already threw inside parseRefreshTokenResponse so the unreachable reject branch misleads debugging; a future reader will assume parse failures are handled there.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh flow checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...`. `statusText` is not a reliable indicator for fetch success (can be empty even on 200), so this can incorrectly throw a 400 on successful responses or miss failures where `statusText` doesn’t match expectations. Also, `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` (added in this PR) throws when `safeParse` fails, so `const accessTokenParsed = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` will never return `{ success: false, ... }`; therefore the subsequent `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) { ... }` branch is dead/unreachable and misleading.
